title: Jamal Edwards' sister on celebrating SBTV's 20-year legacy and hopes of discovering new talent
content:
Launched in the early days of YouTube with homemade videos featuring emerging artists, online music channel SBTV went on to shake up the music industry.
Pioneering DJ and entrepreneur Jamal Edwards founded the grime and rap music platform back in 2006 after he got a camcorder for Christmas and started filming his friends on the council estate where he grew up in west London.
It helped launch the careers of many acts including Dave, Ed Sheeran, Jessie J and Skepta.
By the age of 23, Jamal was a multimillionaire and channelling his success into helping others. He was awarded an MBE for his services to music in 2014.
He died aged 31 in 2022 of cardiac arrhythmia following drug use, prompting a flood of tributes from those who he helped support.
As the channel marks its 20th anniversary, it is set to bring back some of its freestyle formats in the hope of discovering a new generation of rappers.
His sister has been keeping his legacy going by taking over as CEO of SBTV.
Tanisha, who is also a singer-songwriter and producer, feels in a world where algorithms influence what we listen to, it's important to still have platforms curated by music lovers.
"I know how it feels as an artist and trying to put yourself out there and break through those doors," she says.
"So I think it's very key to still have a platform that does want to help up-and-coming talent, that does want to go to places on the map that you wouldn't mainly really go to."
A host of the artists who were platformed on the channel, including Tinie Tempah, Lady Leshurr and Tinchy Stryder, are also set to perform at a one-off show held in London's O2 arena next week to mark the 20-year milestone.
The event, which will also see artists like Dappy, Headie One and Ms Banks take to the stage, will raise money for the Jamal Edwards Self Belief Trust.
Tanisha says being able to honour her brother's legacy "means everything".
"Obviously he's not physically here with us," she says.
"But to be able to carry on his name and carry on the work he did and be able to push his message of self-belief.
"And finding the next generation of talent, working with all these artists that he's previously worked with... I just feel really grateful, honoured and blessed that we're able to continue his name and legacy in such a way."
Rappers Nolay and Griminal are among those who see Jamal as a "catalyst" for their careers and say they're excited to celebrate his impact at the upcoming show.
Griminal recalls how the DJ had a "positive energy and spirit" and an eye for spotting "raw talent".
Nolay tells Newsbeat Jamal not only championed her work, but opened her eyes to the power of promoting your music online and creating a brand for yourself.
Boosting yourself on social media to break into the music industry has become a given in 2026 - something Nolay says has made things feel less "real".

title: The Zombies' Rod Argent back on stage after stroke
content:
The Zombies founding member Rod Argent has returned to the stage for his first live performance in two and a half years after suffering a stroke.
The 81-year-old keyboardist said he had felt "really nervous" before joining bandmate Colin Blunstone at St Albans Cathedral as part of the band's annual Begin Here Festival .
Founded in the Hertfordshire city in 1962, the band most recently became active again in 2004 before stopping after Argent's stroke in July 2024.
"I felt people were all trying to make me feel at home in the best possible way, and then after each song they all stood up and cheered... It was very emotional," he said.
Argent was welcomed to the stage with a standing ovation, with the audience rising again after each song.
Singer Blunstone said: "It was very emotional and I think the crowd felt it and we certainly felt it on stage... It was a wonderful reaction to him.
"They were a wonderful audience. They really, really were and they lifted us... It was very moving."
Argent initially thought he had suffered a transient ischaemic attack before hospital tests confirmed it had been a stroke.
The songwriter said: "In my head, if I'm just thinking through things, I've got absolutely no lack of fluency at all.
"But when I speak, sometimes I lose my thread, lose where I'm going... but it is getting better."
Argent also paid tribute to his wife for her support during his recovery, and said he did not want to tour again.
The songwriter – who also founded the eponymous band Argent – said: "Over the last two years she's been wonderful because she's got a few health issues herself, but she was with me when I had the stroke.
"I want to spend more time with my wife now really, because I was away all the time before."

title: Courteeners to headline the Ludlow Castle concerts
content:
Indie rock band Courteeners are the latest headlining act to be announced for a series of concerts in south Shropshire.
The Manchester-based five piece will be joined by The Coral and The Guest List as supporting acts on Friday 16 July 2027, as part of the annual Live at Ludlow Castle events.
Other headliners already announced for the concert series include McFly, Becky Hill and Paul Heaton.
The band is best known for their 2008 debut album St. Jude, which featured songs Not Nineteen Forever and What Took You So Long.
The album made history in 2023, becoming the album with the longest gap between release and topping the UK chart , at 14 years, 9 months and 7 days.
The band have been together for 20 years, and this year released a new best-of compilation album called God Bless The Band, which they will perform in Ludlow.
They are currently travelling around the country on a tour of the same name.
The greatest hits record features songs from each of their seven albums, which frontman and songwriter Liam Fray said made him reminisce .
The concerts in Ludlow began in 2023, with 50,000 people visiting this year over two weekends, to see the likes of Snow Patrol, Paul Weller, The Human League, Tom Grennan, The Streets, Rick Astley, Richard Ashcroft and Scissor Sisters.
Tickets for the Courteeners will go on sale for people in the local area on 4 November and a general sale on 6 November.
